caption.text:
Every layout in this engine, at the edge of its copy budget, in a single deck.

This is the QA deck: if a headline collides with a number, a tile overflows or a chart axis leaves its card, it shows up here first — and the golden-image test fails before it ships.

slides.headline: Twelve layouts, twelve ways to break a deck
slides.alt_text: Cover: twelve layouts, twelve ways to break a deck.
slides.sub: Maximal copy, longest labels, five steps and nine tiles — all in one deck.

slides.headline: Two claims, one variable flipped
slides.alt_text: Split slide: the old way versus the new way, with a verdict underneath.

left.label: THE OLD WAY
left.text: Write the deck first and fix the layout later.

right.label: THE NEW WAY
right.text: Declare the spec, then render the pixels.

slides.verdict: The variable is who owns the pixels.

slides.headline: Five layers, four active
slides.alt_text: Five stacked layers, four active, with the spec layer highlighted.

slides.headline: Five steps with two-line details
slides.alt_text: Five numbered steps with two-line details.

steps.title: Freeze the fonts
steps.detail: Bundle the TTFs so text cannot reflow on another machine.

steps.title: Read the pixels
steps.detail: The only test that catches collisions.

slides.headline: Nine tiles, six with numbers
slides.alt_text: Nine-tile bento grid, one accent tile, three tiles carrying numbers.

slides.headline: Eight points on one line
slides.alt_text: Line chart of retention across eight slides, rising to 63 percent.

slides.headline: Then the deck has to pay it back immediately
slides.alt_text: Open-loop slide with body copy and a bleeding teaser card.
slides.body: A frame that only sets context asks the reader to invest before giving them a reason. The next slide has to pay that investment back instantly.

slides.headline: A note with every optional field filled
slides.alt_text: Taped note card with a marker highlight and a save prompt.
slides.note: Scrapbook is the layout where imperfection is the point, but the imperfection has to be the same every time — that is what makes it reproducible.

slides.headline: A metric with a long label and a distinct credit
slides.alt_text: Proof slide: 12.4x faster to a rendered deck, with a named source.
slides.metric_label: Faster to a rendered deck than a design tool
slides.finding: Measuring render time against a comparable manual workflow, including the export and the resize.

slides.headline: The twelfth layout draws itself
slides.alt_text: Framed constellation plot of thin lines and mint nodes, above the headline The twelfth layout draws itself.
slides.sub: A seeded plot instead of a stock image: the same QA deck now covers every frame the engine ships.

art clips to the frame, copy keeps its measured height

slides.headline: What to remember
slides.alt_text: Six-bullet recap with a save prompt.
bullets: Every layout has a copy budget

slides.headline: Comment STRESS for the QA deck
slides.alt_text: Comment CTA asking for the keyword STRESS.
slides.text: Comment STRESS and I will send the full stress deck with every spec file included.
